text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High GPU queue growth detected in cluster infer-prod. queue_size=18420 (5m), p95 latency > 12s, HPA (custom-metrics) not increasing replicas. Alert link: https://grafana.internal/alerts/42

Dave-oncall: acked. I'm on call. Pinging SRE + infra. Any immediate customer impact? :phone:

Alice-sre: seeing many pods Pending with FailedScheduling: 0/120 nodes available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu. HPA shows desired=40 but current=12. Custom metrics endpoint returns 500 for adapter.

Carla-enginfra: looking at prometheus-adapter logs now — adapter backlog queue_depth spiked, lots of "timeout waiting for scrape" and 504s to prometheus. metrics-server seems stale for many pods. Possible scrape storm from model-exporter.

Ben-ml: production runtime (infer-runtime) queueing requests, internal queue length per shard > 1k. Upstream client retries causing thundering. We're seeing 429s and some customer-facing timeouts.

Ella-cs: already getting 3 support tickets flagged "inference timeouts" from two mid-market customers, plus a Slack from priority customer BetaCorp. I've asked for proactive comms.

Dave-oncall: immediate plan: 1) add emergency GPU capacity (manual nodegroup scale), 2) restart prometheus-adapter and increase its replicas, 3) temporarily relax low-priority worker tickets and reroute to CPU pool, 4) toggle runtime fallback for small requests. Executing step 1+2 now.

Carla-enginfra: kicking off nodegroup scale via aws-eks. Command: ```eksctl scale nodegroup --cluster infer-prod --name gpu-pool --nodes 8``` estimated join ~6m. Also applying a quick deployment bump for prometheus-adapter: replicas -> 3.

bot-deploy: Deploy started: prometheus-adapter -> replicas=3 by carla-enginfra.

Alice-sre: while nodes come up, we can try to force HPA to see metrics by restarting custom-metrics adapter and checking RBAC errors. I'm running `kubectl rollout restart deploy/prom-adapter -n kube-system`.

Carla-enginfra: prom-adapter pods restarted. Logs show upstream 502 -> prometheus: "exceeded query timeout". Increasing scrape_interval for model-exporter to 30s to reduce load. Also temporarily bumping prom-adapter request_timeouts.

Ben-ml: I've deployed a routing patch to divert embeddings and batch-heavy jobs to the dedicated embeddings pool (cpu-backed) to reduce GPU pressure. Patch applied: `kubectl apply -f routing/priority-divert.yaml`

Dave-oncall: manual nodegroup scale finished, new nodes registered. Kube scheduler placing pods. HPA beginning to react — saw custom metric delta after ~90s. queue_size trending down from 18k -> 9k.

Alice-sre: HPA observed metrics and increased replicas from 12 -> 26, now up to 32 as kube nodes became ready. Some pods still Pending due to GPU allocation fragmentation; evicting low priority pods to defragment.

Ben-ml: after routing change and additional nodes, p95 latency down to ~3.2s. Still seeing some throttling spikes on a few shards; investigating hotspot.

Ella-cs: notified impacted customers with status update, offered interim credits, and set expectation: full recovery window ~30-45m.

Frank-product: heads-up for canary customers and internal dashboards — we might want to pause new signups to avoid re-triggering LB pressure.

Dave-oncall: post-incident notes while still hot: root cause appears to be a scrape storm from model-exporter overload causing prometheus timeouts -> prom-adapter backlog -> stale HPA metrics -> delayed autoscaling -> queue growth -> GPU exhaustion. Immediate mitigations: scale nodes, restart adapter, bump adapter replicas, reduce exporter scrape frequency, reroute heavy workloads, enable CPU fallback.

Carla-enginfra: follow-ups: (1) add autoscaling for prom-adapter, (2) set circuit-breaker alert when adapter queue_depth > 200, (3) tune exporter scrape targets with relabeling to avoid hot paths, (4) improve fragmentation packing/defragmenter for GPU nodes.

Alice-sre: I'll open an incident runbook PR with exact commands and include a checklist for future similar incidents (pre-scale checks, adapter health probe).

Dave-oncall: thanks all. I'll run a retrospective in 48h and invite infra/sre/ml/devex. Marking incident as mitigated but not closed: continuing monitoring for 2h. :white_check_mark:

Ella-cs: updating tickets and the status page now.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by manual scaling and prom-adapter fixes. Please add any additional observations below. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
